title: Tang Yuan Glutinous Rice Balls

seo.title: Tang Yuan Recipe: Authentic Chinese Glutinous Rice Balls
seo.metaDescription: Learn how to make authentic Tang Yuan (Glutinous Rice Balls) with our easy step-by-step recipe. A traditional Chinese dessert perfect for any celebration!

h2Headings: Pro Tips for Perfect Tang Yuan
seo.imageAlt: A bowl of freshly made Tang Yuan (Glutinous Rice Balls) in a sweet ginger soup, garnished with osmanthus flowers.
seo.imageCaption: Enjoy a warm bowl of homemade Tang Yuan, a comforting and traditional Chinese dessert perfect for family gatherings.

description: Tang Yuan are delightful Chinese glutinous rice balls, traditionally enjoyed during festivals like the Lantern Festival and Winter Solstice. These soft, chewy spheres often come with a sweet filling and are served in a warm, comforting soup. They symbolize togetherness and completeness, making them a beloved dessert for family gatherings.

ingredients.notes: also known as sweet rice flour

instructions.title: Prepare the Black Sesame Filling
instructions.text: In a food processor, grind the roasted black sesame seeds until fine. Transfer to a bowl, add granulated sugar and melted lard or butter. Mix well until a thick paste forms. Refrigerate for 15-20 minutes to firm up, then divide into 12-16 small portions and roll into tiny balls.

instructions.title: Make the Glutinous Rice Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, gradually add warm water to the glutinous rice flour, mixing with chopsticks or a spoon. Once it starts to form clumps, use your hands to knead until a smooth, soft, and pliable dough forms. The dough should not be sticky. If it is too dry, add a tiny bit more water; if too wet, add a little more flour.

instructions.title: Form the Tang Yuan Balls
instructions.text: Divide the dough into 12-16 equal portions. Take one portion and flatten it into a small disc in your palm. Place a pre-made sesame filling ball in the center. Carefully cup the dough around the filling and seal it completely, then roll it gently between your palms to form a smooth, round ball. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.

instructions.title: Prepare the Ginger Soup
instructions.text: In a medium pot, bring 800ml of water to a boil. Add ginger slices and rock sugar. Reduce heat to a simmer and let it cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sugar to dissolve completely. Taste and adjust sweetness if necessary.

instructions.title: Cook the Tang Yuan
instructions.text: In a separate large pot, bring plenty of water to a rolling boil. Gently drop the prepared Tang Yuan into the boiling water, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking. Once the Tang Yuan float to the surface, continue to cook for another 2-3 minutes until they are thoroughly cooked and soft. They should appear slightly translucent.

instructions.title: Serve the Tang Yuan
instructions.text: Carefully scoop the cooked Tang Yuan out of the boiling water using a slotted spoon and place them into individual serving bowls. Ladle the hot ginger soup over the Tang Yuan. Garnish with a sprinkle of dried osmanthus flowers if desired, and serve immediately while warm.

tips: When kneading the glutinous rice dough, add water gradually until it reaches an earlobe-like consistency. It should be soft and pliable, not sticky, to prevent cracking when forming balls.
For the filling, ensure the lard or butter is well mixed with the sesame and sugar. Chilling the filling helps it firm up, making it easier to handle and shape into balls.

Tang Yuan are best enjoyed fresh and warm. If you have leftovers, store uncooked Tang Yuan in the freezer on a floured tray before transferring to an airtight container. Cook from frozen directly in boiling water.
